subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Which tool-result visibility policy should OpenClaw use for DeepSeek prefix-cache mitigation: only low-information heartbeat/status outputs, or a broader provider-level placeholder policy for normal tools?
rationale: The code can mechanically summarize selected results, but deciding that normal file, shell, web, or memory outputs may be hidden from the next model turn changes agent behavior and provider payload semantics.

options.title: Narrow to heartbeat/status outputs
options.body: Rebase onto `packages/ai` and summarize only maintainer-approved low-information heartbeat/status results with tests and live/request-shape proof.

options.title: Accept a broader placeholder policy
options.body: Maintainers can deliberately choose to hide additional tool families, but that needs explicit product approval and regression coverage for agent reasoning flows.

options.title: Defer to the canonical issue
options.body: Pause this PR while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97651 owns the remaining tool-result visibility design and live validation.

recommendation.title: Narrow to heartbeat/status outputs
recommendation.body: Rebase onto `packages/ai` and summarize only maintainer-approved low-information heartbeat/status results with tests and live/request-shape proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current provider conversion surface now lives in the AI runtime package he recently extracted and owns historically in this area.
